name: Kids Boo Fest at Six Flags Great America
summary: Kids Boo Fest at Six Flags Great America is the park’s daytime, family-focused Halloween event in 2026. It offers costumes, treats and shows before the more intense Fright Fest program after dark. Check the park calendar because the announced range includes only scheduled event days.
h1: Kids Boo Fest at Six Flags Great America: 2026 dates and family plan
title: Kids Boo Fest at Six Flags Great America
description: Kids Boo Fest at Six Flags Great America in 2026: confirmed dates, daytime activities, age guidance and how to leave before Fright Fest scares begin.

notes: The daytime Halloween program runs with ordinary park admission or an eligible pass on scheduled dates.
Food, merchandise, parking and separately priced activities cost extra; check the official park page before visiting.
The later Fright Fest haunted mazes require a separate Haunted Attractions Pass.

whatYouDont: A promise that the event runs every day within the published range; confirm the selected day on the park calendar.
The after-dark Fright Fest haunted mazes with ordinary daytime admission; that program has a separate maze pass.
A scare-free park after the nighttime Fright Fest program begins.

verdict.short: The family choice at Six Flags Great America if you want Halloween activities without evening scare zones.
worthItIf: Your children want treats, costumes and daytime entertainment.
Your group wants ordinary rides alongside the Halloween activities.
You can arrive while the daytime activities are operating.
skipIf: You are visiting on a day outside the official event schedule.
You want a haunted maze or scare-zone night rather than family activities.
You cannot arrive until daytime programming has ended.

strategy.heading: Check the exact date
body: The official announcement gives a seasonal range but activity dates and park hours vary. Confirm the day and entertainment times on the park calendar before leaving home.

strategy.heading: Do the child activities first
body: Visit the treat trail, costume activity and family shows before moving to rides. Named activities can finish before the park closes.

strategy.heading: Plan the handoff to night
body: Fright Fest is a more intense after-dark program that Six Flags does not recommend for children under 13. Leave before the scare zones become active if your family wants only the daytime event.

faqs.a: The park describes this as a family-friendly daytime Halloween program. The more intense Fright Fest scare zones begin later, so check the day’s transition time and leave beforehand if needed.

faqs.q: Does the daytime event require a separate ticket?
faqs.a: The park markets the event with ordinary park admission on scheduled event days. Check your selected ticket or pass terms and any activity-specific charges before purchasing.
Saturdays and Sundays September 19–November 1, 2026. Check the date-specific calendar before travel; the event does not run on every date in the published range.

faqs.q: Can we stay for Fright Fest afterward?
faqs.a: A standard ticket may cover the general evening scare zones on a scheduled Fright Fest night, but haunted mazes require a separate Haunted Attractions Pass. Six Flags does not recommend the evening event for children under 13.
